terms.meaning: A standard slide type stored in the lessons analysis.
The label saying what kind of slide it is, such as pillar, project or factbase.
One stored point of text on a slide.
The record of where a claim came from.

sections.name: File setup, B, BodyProps, cite, ids
sections.title: Shared types and small helpers
sections.what: Defines what a bullet can be (plain text, or an object with text, fact IDs and a citation) and the inputs this body needs. Two small helpers return a bullet's citation and fact IDs, or nothing for plain text.
sections.why: The header comment says the body shows every stored bullet exactly once, in stored order, with its full text.
sections.watch_out: Plain-text bullets have no citation or fact IDs, so callers must handle empty results.

sections.name: splitLead
sections.title: Lead label splitter
sections.what: Takes bullet text such as 'Label: rest' and separates the label from the rest. If there is no clear label, it returns no label and the full text.
sections.why: The comment says labels are never invented, only taken from existing text.
sections.watch_out: The label must be 3 to 60 characters with no earlier colon. Longer or unusual leads stay as one block of text.

sections.name: bodyScale
sections.title: Text size by length
sections.what: Chooses font size, line spacing and gaps from the total characters on the slide. Shorter text gets larger type, and the longest text gets the smallest tier.
sections.why: Likely reason: longer text must still fit on one slide. The comment mentions a budget of up to 1800 characters.
sections.watch_out: The thresholds were chosen for fit. Changing them can push text off the slide.

sections.name: Sup
sections.title: Reference number marker
sections.what: Shows up to three reference numbers after a bullet, plus a count of any extra ones, for facts that appear in the reference list.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets readers match a bullet to its numbered source.
sections.watch_out: Fact IDs that have no number in the reference list are dropped silently.

sections.name: Edited
sections.title: Edited tag
sections.what: Shows a small red Edited label when a reviewer changed a bullet.
sections.why: Likely reason: flags wording that differs from the original analysis.
sections.watch_out: The tag depends on the edited list passed in. A wrong list puts the tag on the wrong bullets.

sections.name: Txt
sections.title: Bullet text with links
sections.what: Draws one bullet's text as a clickable link that opens its sources. It can show the whole text, only the bold lead, or only the text after the lead, so each layout can place the parts where they fit.
sections.why: The comment says references appear once per bullet, on the body or whole text, and never on the lead.
sections.watch_out: If the lead is requested but none exists, the full text is shown instead.

sections.name: LabelledRows
sections.title: Labelled rows layout
sections.what: Lays bullets out as rows with the bold label in a left column and the body on the right. Rows stretch to fill the page when there is little text. Bullets without a lead show a number instead.
sections.why: Likely reason: suits slides where each point has a heading. Not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The left column has a fixed pixel width, so long labels wrap heavily on narrow pages.

sections.name: Cards
sections.title: Card layout
sections.what: Shows bullets as boxes in a grid, each with a red top edge and an optional bold label above the body.
sections.why: Likely reason: suits framework and example slides where each item stands on its own.
sections.watch_out: The caller chooses the number of columns. Many bullets make very small cards.

sections.name: Numbered
sections.title: Numbered list layout
sections.what: Shows bullets as a numbered list that can flow into two columns when the text is long. Each item stays together when a column breaks.
sections.why: Likely reason: source and fact lists read best as numbered entries.
sections.watch_out: Numbers come from the stored position, so they stay aligned with the stored order.

sections.name: CanonicalBody
sections.title: Main body chooser
sections.what: Chooses the layout from the profile name. Project slides put the first bullet in a highlighted box beside labelled rows. Framework, examples, factbase, source, matrix and other profiles each get their own layout. Bullets from the chart start index onward are listed under Chart datapoints. Only the first part of this section was in the packet; the last few lines were not provided.
sections.why: The header comment says structure comes only from the profile.
sections.watch_out: Profile matching ignores letter case. Unknown profiles fall back to the default labelled rows.

summary: Draws the main text area of a canonical lessons slide, arranging each stored bullet in a layout chosen by the slide's profile type.
purpose: Show every stored bullet on a slide, with its sources, in a layout that suits the slide type.
why: The header comment says structure comes only from the profile and from existing 'Label: body' text, so nothing is invented. The reason is otherwise not stated.
how: 1. Splits the bullets into the main list and the chart datapoints, starting at the chart start index. 2. Adds up the characters to choose a text size. 3. Picks a layout by profile name. 4. Lists chart datapoints below the main body. 5. Draws each bullet as a clickable link to its sources, with a reference number and an Edited tag if it was changed.
inputs: profile (text), bullets (plain text or objects with text, fact IDs and a citation), chartFrom (number), edited (list of positions), refIndex (map from fact ID to reference number).
outputs: Rendered text blocks on the slide. No data is changed.
risks: Profile names are matched in lower case, and an unknown profile falls back to the default layout without an error. Edited tags and reference numbers depend on correct positions and IDs. The end of the file was not in the packet, so its closing part is unverified.
debug: If a slide looks wrong, check the profile value and the chart start index first. If a reference number is missing, check that its fact ID is in refIndex. If text looks cramped or cut off, check the size tier chosen from the character count.
